sentences.text: Charts and books go out of date the day they’re printed.
Notices to Mariners keep them current.
The Local Notice to Mariners comes out weekly from each Coast Guard district.
This is the one you’ll actually use.
It lists aids that have been added, moved, or are off station, plus dredging, construction, marine events, hazards, and chart corrections for local waters.
The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency publishes its own weekly Notice to Mariners, for ocean charts and international publications.
And for things that can’t wait a week, the Coast Guard makes Broadcast Notices to Mariners.
They’re announced on channel sixteen, and then read on channel twenty-two alpha.
So when you hear the Coast Guard say, switch to twenty-two alpha, what should you do?
It may be about the channel you’re in.
